walkthroughs.body_html:
Fine Art — a core area of A-Level Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fine Art brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fine Art.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which painter is most associated with thick impasto self-portraits in mid-twentieth century Britain?
options: David Hockney
Frank Auerbach
Howard Hodgkin
Patrick Heron

mcqs.q: Which medium did David Hockney use for his iconic 1967 'A Bigger Splash'?
options: Oil
Acrylic
Watercolour
Tempera

mcqs.q: What did Renaissance artists rediscover that medieval art lacked?
options: It rejects all modern imagery.
Painting on canvas.
Linear perspective and naturalistic representation of the human body.
The use of colour.

mcqs.q: What attitude does Pop Art take toward consumer culture?
options: Painting on canvas.
It rejects all modern imagery.
Ambiguous - it both celebrates and critiques mass media imagery.
It straightforwardly celebrates capitalism.

mcqs.q: What is appropriation in postmodern art?
options: Deliberately reusing existing images or styles, often to comment on originality.
Painting in an old-fashioned style.
Stealing artwork to sell.
It rejects all modern imagery.
